asr.text: Good afternoon, Kalish. Hope your Sunday has been an easy one.
asr.review: accepted: place name Caliche transcribed as 'Kalish'; all other words exact. Seeds 43-47 gave Kalish/Kelly/Colleague; I10_BACK_ON_ROAD_001 seed 44 was heard as 'Caliche'.

asr.text: We've still got a little sunshine left. Good time to get the washing off the line.
A reminder from the feed store. Tomorrow's delivery comes in after 10. Let them have their coffee first.
And if you're heading out to work, the diner has the griddle on.
Take it easy through town. There's no prize for getting to the next red light first.
Here's another record for the road.
Hi there, sit wherever you like.
Kitchen's still going. Coffee's fresh enough that I can say it with a straight face.
You want to see the menu or are you just stretching your legs?
Burger comes with fries. Sandwich comes with chips.
Coffee with either one. I can wrap the food if you're taking it to work.
What sounds good.
One burger, fries and coffee coming right up.
There you go. Careful with the plate.
Eating here, or shall I wrap it?
Sandwich chips and coffee. You got it.
Here we are, napkins are right beside you.
Staying for a minute or taking that along.
Sure. Take your time.
Mind if I top that coffee up?
There. That should keep you going.
Thanks for stopping in. Have a good shift.
No trouble. I'll put it in a bag.
Fork and napkins are in there. Coffee's got a lid.
Keep the bag upright, the bottom's got more confidence than strength.
Have a good evening out there.
Of course, here you are.
You've caught us between the supper crowd and the coffee crowd.
Nice having a minute to wipe a table before somebody needs it.
Let me know if you change your mind about food.
Alright, thanks for coming in.
We're here if you need something later.
Drive safely.
You're listening to local radio here in Caliche.
Church supper volunteers, your pans are clean and waiting in the kitchen. Please take yours home before somebody makes another casserole in it.
We'll leave you with some music now.
Good evening to everybody starting work and everybody heading home.
Hi again, back from Sorrow.
asr.review: accepted: station name SARO transcribed as 'Sorrow' (spoken as a word, not spelled).

asr.text: Coffee's on. You can sit down a minute.
That driver came in a little while ago. He's over there if you're looking for somebody who's been on the road.
There's a paper on the counter too. Nobody's claimed it.
Evening coming in from work.
Take a seat if you need one. Coffee's on.
That fellow over there just came off the road. He's been sitting with his cup for a while.
Papers on the counter if you want something to read.
Keep on through town then take the marked turn out to the array.
Big sign, hard to miss unless you're arguing with the radio.
You'll want to eat before you get settled in out there.
Want the menu before you go?
If you're hungry the burger.
If you're driving the sandwiches less of a project.
Either way, I'm putting napkins in the bag.
Your call.
Reyes, Dale, the logbook should be in front of you.
I headed out early! The service folder is on the desk, under the work order!
The first survey is routine. Check calibration before you let it run.
Did you get something to eat?
Good. Better than trying to live on the coffee here.
Try that once. Wouldn't recommend it!
asr.review: unresolved: 'I tried that once' heard as 'Try that once' in seeds 42-48, 14 probe variants and in context after D01_FOOD_001. The opening 'I' is probably fused or swallowed. Needs listening; re-record or rewrite the line if it is audibly missing.

asr.text: There are crackers in the bottom drawer, still in the wrapper!
No promises about the coffee! It was here when I came in!
Start with the log. I've marked what's done and what's left for you.
Bank 3 has two amber indicators. Amber is normal. Write it down if that changes.
Your folder lists the local service records and the radio schedule. Get the dated copies. We need something to check our clocks against.
Operations office is locked. The papers for tonight are already on your desk.
Ward is on call for the morning run. She wants observation she can sign, not our best guess.
asr.review: unresolved: 'observations she' heard as 'observation she' (s/sh merge or dropped plural). Seeds 42-48 all have it or mishear Ward; also in context. Needs listening.

asr.text: You can reach me on the service line. If something doesn't fit the log, call before you throw anything away.
All right, have a good shift.
Dale, you have the service sheet!
Then start with the feeder marked on that sheet. A receiver warning and a supply fault are two different things.
The junction station is down the short gravel turnoff. Leave the truck outside the service gate.
Use the service check on the cabinet, note what the affected light does, not just what the indicator says.
There should be one clear result. If the result is not clear, leave it unresolved and call me.
I hear you. Check the cabinet label against the service sheet.
If they match, run the check and watch the light at the far end.
Write down the result and the time. Keep that for the next check.
Dale, what did it actually print?
Minus 39, on the paper!
Keep the original. Put the clock reading beside it before you do anything else.
Do not correct the number, just because it looks wrong!
I've seen numbers that shouldn't have come out of that solver.
I haven't worked out why! I kept the records!
Keep yours too! We can argue about the explanation later!
Check your inspection card! Put the test time beside the new printout!
If you've cleared the supply fault, compare that time with this one.
Alright, put the paper somewhere safe!
Call me if the next observation disagrees with the first one.
You found a spare!
I should have told you there was more than a service folder!
What are you looking at?
Ward wants a result. Somebody else can repeat. She's right too.
asr.review: accepted: homophone 'right to' / 'right too'; same words otherwise (ASR sentence split only).

asr.text: I had clippings, bad frames, and people who remembered different nights.
I kept the lot until I could put two observations on the same page.
Watch the pole, not the patch!
The patch could be a recording fault. The poll gives you a fixed reference.
Use the field sheet! I marked the camera position.
I haven't worked through those survey files.
The folder in my office is my own. I haven't changed an old report.
Keep the originals together! Check whose name is on the signed copy!
Start with one thing you can check. Take a photograph from the same place.
And don't take my word for something just because I wrote it down.
Say that again! The service result and the light disagree!
You checked the ordinary supply, the backup, and the indicator?
Good. Write down every check you made. Keep that separate from what you think caused it.
Bring the record back to sorrow. Ward will need to read it.
asr.review: accepted: SARO transcribed as 'sorrow', as in I12.

asr.text: Reyes! I'm here!
If you've got witness statements, keep their exact words with the record.
Give Ward what you've actually checked! Leave the rest marked uncertain!
Call me when you get back in!
